_comment: Digest of the migration chain reviewed for outbound behaviour. Re-pin only after reviewing the diff.

reviews.units: U1a, U1b, U1c prereqs 1-4 (#641-#646, already merged to main) and U2 incl. slice A (#647)

outbound_sweep.method: every sanitizer sweep pattern applied to all 19 added migrations: cron.schedule, cron.alter_job, net.http_post, net.http_request_queue, supabase_functions.http_request, extensions.http_, dblink, CREATE FOREIGN TABLE/SERVER, schedule_in_database, vault.*, CREATE EXTENSION, pg_read_, COPY
outbound_sweep.new_outbound_capable_functions: none — no added migration defines a function that reaches net.http_post, supabase_functions.http_request, dblink or extensions.http_*, so reviewed-outbound-functions.tsv is unchanged
outbound_sweep.new_extensions: none — no added migration issues CREATE EXTENSION, so reviewed-extensions.tsv is unchanged
outbound_sweep.false_positives_checked: the only COPY hit (20261117100000) is the word 'copy' inside a prose comment, not a COPY command

why_the_sanitized_clone_stays_outbound_i: The single outbound-capable migration schedules a cron job whose command contains net.http_post. That call lives inside a $cmd$ STRING LITERAL: it is stored, never executed at apply time, so applying the chain issues no request.

On a rehearsal target pg_cron and pg_net are never installed — the sanitizer neutralises their CREATE EXTENSION statements — and sql/platform_stub.sql supplies inert cron/net objects instead. There is no scheduler process, so a stored command can never tick.

The stub's cron.schedule INSERTs with active = false, and its cron.alter_job hard-codes active = false on every call. A job created through the stub therefore cannot be armed even by a migration that tried to arm one. This migration also disables the job itself, so the two agree.
The stub's net.http_post is inert and records into net.blocked_outbound_attempts rather than emitting anything.

The migration's Vault read resolves against the stub's vault.decrypted_secrets view. It finds no service_role_key on a rehearsal target, which this migration handles by installing the job anyway (deliberately: an apply-time skip would record the migration as applied while creating nothing).
The stub's cron.job carries the username column and cron.schedule returns bigint, so this migration's owner-scoped lookup and its use of the returned jobid both work unchanged on a sanitized target.
inventories_updated: reviewed-cron-jobs.tsv — added notification-identity-worker, outbound=yes (the column classifies the stored command, not whether the job is armed; it ships INACTIVE)
reviewed-outbound-functions.tsv — unchanged, no new outbound-capable functions
